newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady on Thursday in moderate trade, dealers said.

They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. weekly jobless claims, June housing starts and the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia July survey of regional business activity data.
Weekly jobless claims for the week ending July 12 are forecast to be around 345,000 compared with 377,000 reported in the previous week.
Housing starts for June is expected to be around 1.45 million annualised units against May's 1.397 million units.
The Philadelphia Fed July index is expected to come out with a reading of 18 from 25.2 in the previous report.

"The market was quietly steady in the morning except for some position adjustments at the short end. Some people are waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the weekly jobless claims, housing starts and Philadelphia Fed survey figures," a local dealer said.
"But the numbers have beeb built into the market and most people have squared their positions for the day, so I don't think there will be much impact," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Thursday/Friday and week-fixed were unchanged from Wednesday's common 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent, respectively.
Week-fixed rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.

Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged from Wednesday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8, six-months unchanged at 5-7/8 5-3/4 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/16 5-15/16 percent.
